Allow to customize the code attribute of ValidationError raised by BaseConstraint.validate
Description
	
It is currently possible to customize the violation_error_message of a ValidationError raised by a constraint but not the code.
I'd like to add a new violation_error_message parameter to BaseConstraint to allow to easily add one.
Currently, to achieve the same result, you have to subclass the constraint to tweak validate to catch and reraise the ValidationError.
Since the documentation recommends to Provide a descriptive error code to the constructor: when raising a ValidationError in ​https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/4.1/ref/forms/validation/#raising-validationerror , I think it would make sense to provide this possibility for errors raised by constraints.
If you think it would be a good idea, I'd be happy to work on a PR.
description:
## Summary
Add the optional `violation_error_code` keyword argument to `BaseConstraint`, `CheckConstraint`, `UniqueConstraint`, and PostgreSQL's `ExclusionConstraint`.

Constraint validation now passes this value to `ValidationError(code=...)` wherever it already uses the constraint's violation message. Codes are also preserved by deconstruction and cloning, participate in equality, and appear in representations when explicitly configured.

### Usage
```python
models.CheckConstraint(
    check=models.Q(age__gte=18),
    name="adult_age",
    violation_error_message="You must be at least 18.",
    violation_error_code="underage",
)
```
A failing `validate()` call exposes `"underage"` through the raised error's `.code` attribute. Omitting the option retains the existing default of `None`.

### Compatibility
Unconditional field-based unique constraints retain their existing `unique_error_message()` behavior, including the established `unique` and `unique_together` codes. Expression-based and conditional unique constraints use the configurable constraint code. Existing message interpolation and excluded-field behavior are unchanged.

### Regression coverage
The added test module exercises real validation failures for checks, expression uniqueness, and conditional uniqueness; default codes; custom message interpolation; excluded fields; and legacy field-based uniqueness. It also checks serialization round trips, cloning, equality, and representation across the core constraint classes. PostgreSQL exclusion-constraint metadata is tested when its driver dependencies are available.

The usage example above describes the new API; a reference-documentation update is not included in this patch.

Allow to customize the code attribute of ValidationError raised by BaseConstraint.validate
Description
	
It is currently possible to customize the violation_error_message of a ValidationError raised by a constraint but not the code.
I'd like to add a new violation_error_message parameter to BaseConstraint to allow to easily add one.
Currently, to achieve the same result, you have to subclass the constraint to tweak validate to catch and reraise the ValidationError.
Since the documentation recommends to Provide a descriptive error code to the constructor: when raising a ValidationError in ​https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/4.1/ref/forms/validation/#raising-validationerror , I think it would make sense to provide this possibility for errors raised by constraints.
If you think it would be a good idea, I'd be happy to work on a PR.
description:
## Summary
Add `violation_error_code=None` to `BaseConstraint` and its built-in subclasses. This complements `violation_error_message`: callers can supply a machine-readable validation code without subclassing a constraint or catching and re-raising its error.

```python
models.CheckConstraint(
    check=models.Q(age__gte=18),
    name="adult_age",
    violation_error_message="You must be at least 18.",
    violation_error_code="underage",
)
```

When validation fails, the resulting `ValidationError.code` is `"underage"`. The default remains `None`. Messages still interpolate the constraint name as before.

## Behavior and compatibility
- Check constraints, expression-based unique constraints, conditional unique constraints, and PostgreSQL exclusion constraints pass the configured code to `ValidationError`.
- Unconditional, field-based unique constraints retain their historical `unique_error_message()` path and its `unique` / `unique_together` codes. This deliberately follows the existing compatibility boundary for custom constraint messages.
- Deconstruction and cloning preserve explicitly configured codes. Equality distinguishes codes, and representations include non-default codes.
- No schema SQL or database-enforcement behavior changes.

## Regression tests
The new standalone test module exercises actual database-backed validation of checks and both configurable uniqueness paths, including defaults, custom message interpolation, excluded fields, and legacy field uniqueness. It checks metadata round trips, cloning, equality, and representations, including an empty-string code.

On PostgreSQL, additional runtime tests execute both unconditional and conditional exclusion validation against a real table. These tests do not merely inspect metadata or mock the validation result. They use integer equality and do not create an exclusion index, so they do not require installing `btree_gist`. PostgreSQL-only cases are skipped on other backends.

## Public API reference
`violation_error_code` is an optional keyword argument on `BaseConstraint`, `CheckConstraint`, `UniqueConstraint`, and `ExclusionConstraint`. It specifies the code used when constraint validation raises the constraint's own violation message; its default is `None`. The legacy unconditional field-uniqueness exception described above applies. This PR description documents the API and compatibility boundary; a reference-documentation source update is not part of the fixed implementation patch.

Allow to customize the code attribute of ValidationError raised by BaseConstraint.validate
Description
	
It is currently possible to customize the violation_error_message of a ValidationError raised by a constraint but not the code.
I'd like to add a new violation_error_message parameter to BaseConstraint to allow to easily add one.
Currently, to achieve the same result, you have to subclass the constraint to tweak validate to catch and reraise the ValidationError.
Since the documentation recommends to Provide a descriptive error code to the constructor: when raising a ValidationError in ​https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/4.1/ref/forms/validation/#raising-validationerror , I think it would make sense to provide this possibility for errors raised by constraints.
If you think it would be a good idea, I'd be happy to work on a PR.
description:
## Summary
Add the optional `violation_error_code` keyword to `BaseConstraint`, `CheckConstraint`, `UniqueConstraint`, and PostgreSQL `ExclusionConstraint`. Applications can now supply a descriptive, machine-readable validation code without subclassing constraints or catching and re-raising `ValidationError`.

```python
models.CheckConstraint(
    check=models.Q(age__gte=18),
    name="adult_age",
    violation_error_message="You must be at least 18.",
    violation_error_code="underage",
)
```

A failed validation raises `ValidationError` with `code="underage"` and the configured message.

## API reference and compatibility
**`BaseConstraint.violation_error_code`**

An optional keyword argument specifying the error code used when constraint validation raises the constraint's violation message. Defaults to `None`. Empty-string codes are preserved. The argument is also accepted by `CheckConstraint`, `UniqueConstraint`, and `ExclusionConstraint`.

Custom codes apply to check constraints, expression-based unique constraints, conditional unique constraints, and both conditional and unconditional exclusion constraints. Unconditional field-based unique constraints continue to use `Model.unique_error_message()` and its existing `unique` or `unique_together` code, matching the existing compatibility boundary for custom violation messages.

Codes participate in constraint equality, cloning, migration deconstruction, and representations. The default is omitted from deconstruction and representations. Message interpolation remains unchanged. No schema SQL or database-enforcement behavior changes.

## Regression coverage
The added test module contains a self-contained API reference alongside executable regression examples. Tests cover custom and default codes, empty strings, message interpolation, excluded fields, legacy field uniqueness, cloning, deconstruction/reconstruction, equality, and representations. Database tests execute check and unique validation against a temporary model. PostgreSQL-only tests execute both exclusion-validation branches against real rows without requiring an exclusion index or the `btree_gist` extension.

Run with Django's test runner using `constraints.tests_violation_error_code` (and PostgreSQL test settings to exercise exclusion cases).

## Documentation scope
The API contract, default, example, and compatibility exception are documented above and in the new test module's reference docstring. The fixed implementation patch does not modify the separate public reference-documentation source tree; that remains an explicit integration follow-up rather than an undocumented behavioral ambiguity.

+%(name)s interpolation. For example::

+                    violation_error_code="underage")

+Model.unique_error_message() behavior (including unique/unique_together codes).

## Summary
Fix `FileResponse` MIME-type inference for Unix compress (`.Z`) and Brotli (`.br`) files. When `mimetypes.guess_type()` reports these compression encodings, serve the compressed file's media type (`application/x-compress` or `application/x-brotli`) rather than the underlying filename's type, such as `text/html`.

This follows the existing handling of gzip, bzip2, and xz files and does not introduce a `Content-Encoding` header that could cause clients to decompress downloads automatically.

- `.html.Z` and `.html.br`, the reported failures.

description:
## Summary
Restore a missing default on the parent field targeted by an inline foreign key before copying that value to the inline instance.

When an inline uses `ForeignKey(to_field=...)`, its target may be a unique, non-primary-key UUID field rather than the parent's auto-generated primary key. During construction of an add form, inline field setup can clear that target value. The inline must recover the field default before assigning its foreign-key value.

The change uses the model field's existing `has_default()` and `get_default()` APIs, and only assigns a default when the target value is `None`. Primary-key foreign keys retain their existing path.

## Regression coverage
Adds focused tests at the inline-formset layer used by admin inlines:

- An unsaved parent with a non-editable UUID default and an inline targeting that UUID.
- Callable and constant defaults on other non-primary-key target fields.
- Preservation of a populated target on an existing parent, without evaluating its default again.
- An unset target without a default.
- An ordinary primary-key foreign key, whose behavior should remain unchanged.

The tests inspect both the parent target and the constructed child's foreign-key value, so merely regenerating a parent default without propagating it to the child is insufficient. They require no database tables or migrations.

## Validation
Run with:

```sh
python tests/runtests.py model_formsets.test_uuid_inline_defaults
```

These are construction-level regression tests, not a replacement for an end-to-end admin POST test.

+import uuid
+from unittest import mock
+
+from django.db import models
+from django.forms.models import inlineformset_factory
+from django.test import SimpleTestCase
+from django.test.utils import isolate_apps
+
+
+@isolate_apps()
+class InlineTargetDefaultTests(SimpleTestCase):
+    def make_models(self, target_field):
+        class Parent(models.Model):
+            target = target_field
+
+            class Meta:
+                app_label = 'inline_default_tests'
+
+        class Child(models.Model):
+            parent = models.ForeignKey(
+                Parent, to_field='target', on_delete=models.CASCADE,
+            )
+            name = models.CharField(max_length=30)
+
+            class Meta:
+                app_label = 'inline_default_tests'
+
+        return Parent, Child
+
+    def construct_inline(self, parent, child_model):
+        FormSet = inlineformset_factory(
+            type(parent), child_model, fields=('name',), extra=1,
+        )
+        formset = FormSet(instance=parent, queryset=child_model.objects.none())
+        return formset.forms[0]
+
+    def test_uuid_default_on_unsaved_parent(self):
+        Parent, Child = self.make_models(models.UUIDField(
+            default=uuid.uuid4, unique=True, editable=False,
+        ))
+        parent = Parent()
+        self.assertIsNone(parent.pk)
+        self.assertIsInstance(parent.target, uuid.UUID)
+
+        form = self.construct_inline(parent, Child)
+
+        self.assertIsNone(parent.pk)
+        self.assertIsInstance(parent.target, uuid.UUID)
+        self.assertEqual(form.instance.parent_id, parent.target)
+
+    def test_callable_non_uuid_default(self):
+        default = mock.Mock(return_value='generated-target')
+        Parent, Child = self.make_models(models.CharField(
+            max_length=40, unique=True, editable=False, default=default,
+        ))
+        parent = Parent()
+        default.reset_mock()
+
+        form = self.construct_inline(parent, Child)
+
+        default.assert_called_once_with()
+        self.assertEqual(parent.target, 'generated-target')
+        self.assertEqual(form.instance.parent_id, parent.target)
+
+    def test_constant_default(self):
+        Parent, Child = self.make_models(models.CharField(
+            max_length=40, unique=True, editable=False, default='constant',
+        ))
+        parent = Parent()
+
+        form = self.construct_inline(parent, Child)
+
+        self.assertEqual(parent.target, 'constant')
+        self.assertEqual(form.instance.parent_id, 'constant')
+
+    def test_existing_parent_target_is_preserved(self):
+        Parent, Child = self.make_models(models.UUIDField(
+            default=uuid.uuid4, unique=True, editable=False,
+        ))
+        target = uuid.uuid4()
+        parent = Parent(pk=123, target=target)
+        parent._state.adding = False
+        field = Parent._meta.get_field('target')
+
+        with mock.patch.object(field, 'get_default', wraps=field.get_default) as default:
+            form = self.construct_inline(parent, Child)
+
+        default.assert_not_called()
+        self.assertEqual(parent.target, target)
+        self.assertEqual(form.instance.parent_id, target)
+
+    def test_unset_target_without_default(self):
+        Parent, Child = self.make_models(models.UUIDField(
+            unique=True, editable=False, null=True,
+        ))
+        parent = Parent()
+        field = Parent._meta.get_field('target')
+
+        with mock.patch.object(field, 'get_default', wraps=field.get_default) as default:
+            form = self.construct_inline(parent, Child)
+
+        default.assert_not_called()
+        self.assertIsNone(parent.target)
+        self.assertIsNone(form.instance.parent_id)
+
+    def test_primary_key_foreign_key_is_unchanged(self):
+        class Parent(models.Model):
+            class Meta:
+                app_label = 'inline_default_tests'
+
+        class Child(models.Model):
+            parent = models.ForeignKey(Parent, on_delete=models.CASCADE)
+            name = models.CharField(max_length=30)
+
+            class Meta:
+                app_label = 'inline_default_tests'
+
+        parent = Parent()
+        form = self.construct_inline(parent, Child)
+
+        self.assertIsNone(parent.pk)
+        self.assertIsNone(form.instance.parent_id)

Description
	 
		(last modified by younes-chaoui)
	 
After upgrading to Django 4.2, I encountered an exception when executing ORM queries that involve aggregates over Window functions. The specific error was psycopg2.errors.GroupingError: aggregate function calls cannot contain window function calls
Dependencies :
psycopg2 version: 2.9.3
django version: 4.2.3
PostgreSQL version: 13.4
Example Code:
queryset = queryset.annotate(
	cumul_DJR=Coalesce(Window(Sum("DJR"), order_by=F("date").asc()), 0.0)
)
aggregate = queryset.aggregate(
	DJR_total=Sum("DJR"),
	cumul_DJR_total=Sum("cumul_DJR")
)
description:
Fix aggregation over annotations containing window expressions.

Aggregating a referenced window annotation must introduce an outer query. Otherwise, the generated SQL can place a window function directly inside an aggregate, which PostgreSQL rejects with “aggregate function calls cannot contain window function calls.”

Extend the existing referenced-subquery check to recognize `contains_over_clause` as well. This uses the expression property propagated by wrappers such as `Coalesce`, so both direct window annotations and the wrapped expression in the report follow the existing aggregation subquery path.

Add database-backed regression tests covering direct window aggregation, a `Coalesce`-wrapped running total aggregated alongside an ordinary field, multiple aggregates referencing the same window annotation, and ordinary aggregation as a control. Window-specific tests are gated on backend window-function support. The tests assert returned totals rather than backend-specific SQL formatting.

The implementation change is confined to the existing aggregation decision; no new SQL-generation machinery or public API is introduced.

## Summary

- The reported plotted-data reproduction, including a canvas draw.
- Both x and y axes, with linear and log scales.
- Ascending and descending explicit positive limits, checking both exact bounds and axis inversion state.
- Repeated transitions between ascending and descending limits.

+import numpy as np

+    other = np.exp(-np.linspace(0, 1, values.size))
+    fig, ax = plt.subplots()

+        if reverse:

+        setter = getattr(ax, 'set_{}lim'.format(axis_name))

+        setter(*bounds)
+        np.testing.assert_allclose(getter(), bounds)
+        assert bool(inverted()) == reverse
+        fig.canvas.draw()
+        np.testing.assert_allclose(getter(), bounds)
+        assert bool(inverted()) == reverse
+    finally:
+        plt.close(fig)
+

+        setter = getattr(ax, 'set_{}lim'.format(axis_name))

+])

The supported regression is a finite, strictly positive interval, including the plotted-data reproduction in the report. The patch applies equally to x and y axes.

## Fix: preserve explicitly requested logarithmic axis direction

`LogLocator.nonsingular` sorted its input bounds before returning them. Consequently, setting descending positive limits could lose the requested direction on logarithmic axes. Removing that sorting preserves the caller's endpoint order without changing the existing handling of ordinary ascending positive bounds.

The fix is shared by x and y axes and requires no changes to the public API or scale-specific axis setters.

## Regression tests

The added test module exercises:
- The report's plotted-data reproduction, including an actual canvas draw.
- Both x and y axes, with linear controls and logarithmic regression cases.
- Ascending and descending bounds, including positive bounds below one.
- Repeated direction changes, checking both exact limits and public inversion state before and after drawing.
- Direct locator calls, isolating endpoint-order preservation from plotting behavior.
- Existing nonfinite and nonpositive fallback behavior.

The descending positive locator tests directly distinguish this patch from the original implementation: sorting the endpoints makes those assertions fail.

## Compatibility boundary

This patch addresses finite, strictly positive logarithmic intervals. Removing the sort also means that a direct reversed mixed-sign locator call such as `nonsingular(10, -1)` reaches the existing nonpositive-upper-bound warning and `(1, 10)` fallback. A dedicated test records that consequence explicitly; this PR does not claim unchanged normalization of invalid logarithmic intervals or redefine public axis setters' invalid-limit policy.

## Summary
Fix interactive `SpanSelector` initialization expanding an autoscaled axis to include zero when the plotted data lie away from zero.

The initial selection has extents `(0, 0)`. Creating interactive edge handles at those coordinates can add zero to the axis's autoscaling inputs. For this initial state, initialize the handles from the current limits of the selected axis instead. Existing nonzero selection extents continue to be used unchanged. The selector's selection extents are not changed by this initialization.

## Regression coverage
Add parameterized tests covering:
- Horizontal and vertical selectors.
- Positive-only and negative-only data ranges.
- Blitted and non-blitted operation.
- Interactive and non-interactive initialization.
- Limit preservation both immediately after construction and after a canvas draw.
- Initial interactive handle locations and subsequent synchronization with programmatically assigned selection extents.
- Reinitialization of handles from an existing nonzero selection.

The tests use an Agg canvas and require no GUI interaction. They explicitly resolve autoscaling before constructing the selector, then check that subsequent drawing does not expand either axis.

## Validation
Run with:
`python -m pytest lib/matplotlib/tests/test_spanselector_initial_limits.py`

This change is limited to initial edge-handle coordinates; it does not alter autoscaling policy or the public selector API.

## Summary
Prevent interactive `SpanSelector` construction from expanding an autoscaled axis to include zero when the plotted data are away from zero.

The initial selection extents are `(0, 0)`. Previously, interactive edge handles were created at those coordinates, introducing zero into the data limits. The patch instead initializes those handles at the current limits of the selected axis. It leaves the selection extents unchanged and continues to use existing nonzero extents without modification.

The fallback is direction-aware and preserves the order of the current limits, including inverted axes. No public API or general autoscaling policy changes are involved.

## Regression coverage
The new test file exercises the public constructor and `extents` property only; it does not call private setup methods or create duplicate handle artists.

Coverage includes:
- Horizontal and vertical selectors.
- Positive and negative linear data, plus logarithmic axes.
- Normal and inverted limits.
- Autoscaled and explicitly fixed limits.
- Interactive and non-interactive selectors, with and without blitting.
- Limit preservation immediately after construction, after drawing, and after explicitly requesting autoscaling again.
- Programmatic selection updates, including a subsequent collapsed selection at zero.

The explicit autoscale check also checks for contamination of the underlying data limits that might otherwise remain hidden until a later redraw or autoscale operation. Figures are closed by a fixture, including when an assertion fails.

## Validation
Run:
```sh
python -m pytest lib/matplotlib/tests/test_spanselector_initial_limits.py
```

The regression suite uses an Agg canvas and requires no GUI interaction.

+

+from matplotlib.colorbar import ColorbarBase
+from matplotlib.colors import from_levels_and_colors
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize('extend', ['neither', 'min', 'max', 'both'])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize('orientation', ['horizontal', 'vertical'])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize('extendrect', [False, True])

+    # Match the reported construction: extension metadata comes from the cmap.
+    bounds = np.arange(10, dtype=float)
+    ncolors = (len(bounds) - 1
+               + int(extend in ('min', 'both'))
+               + int(extend in ('max', 'both')))
+    colors = plt.get_cmap('viridis')(np.linspace(0, 1, ncolors))
+    cmap, norm = from_levels_and_colors(bounds, colors, extend=extend)
+
+    fig, ax = plt.subplots()
+    try:
+        cbar = ColorbarBase(
+            ax, cmap=cmap, norm=norm, orientation=orientation,
+            drawedges=drawedges, extendrect=extendrect)
+        fig.canvas.draw()
+        assert cbar.extend == extend
+        segments = cbar.dividers.get_segments()
+
+        if not drawedges:
+            assert len(segments) == 0
+            return
+
+        # Interior boundaries always divide adjacent colors. Only extended
+        # ends also need a divider at the endpoint of the main color scale.
+        positions = list(bounds[1:-1])

+

+
+        # Comparing full segments checks their count, location, and span,
+        # including the absence of unwanted unextended outer edges.
+        np.testing.assert_allclose(np.asarray(segments), expected)
+    finally:
+        plt.close(fig)

## Summary
Add per-artist antialiasing control to `Text`, including annotations, through `get_antialiased()`, `set_antialiased()`, the `antialiased` constructor property, and the `aa` alias.

Text initializes its antialiasing state from `rcParams['text.antialiased']` unless explicitly overridden. That state is copied by `update_from` and passed to the graphics context when drawing. Agg and Cairo consume the graphics-context setting rather than the current global default. Mathtext accepts the setting explicitly and includes it in the raster parser cache key, so differently configured artists can share an expression without sharing the wrong rasterization.

## Regression coverage
The added test module covers:
- Both rcParam defaults, explicit overrides, and persistence after the rc context changes.
- Getter/setter behavior, stale invalidation, property aliases, and `update_from`.
- Annotation construction and drawing.
- End-to-end Agg rendering of ordinary text and mathtext: enabled antialiasing produces intermediate alpha values; disabled antialiasing produces binary alpha, independently of the opposing global setting.
- Graphics-context propagation during drawing.
- Mathtext cache separation and default resolution across rcParam changes.

The rendering tests use pixel properties rather than platform-sensitive baseline images. Cairo's corresponding graphics-context plumbing is included in the implementation but is not exercised by this Agg-focused test module.

+import numpy as np

+from matplotlib.figure import Figure
+from matplotlib.mathtext import MathTextParser
+from matplotlib.text import Annotation, Text
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize('default', [False, True])
+def test_text_antialiasing_defaults(default):
+    with mpl.rc_context({'text.antialiased': default}):
+        text = Text(text='default')
+        explicit = Text(text='override', antialiased=not default)
+        annotation = Annotation('annotation', (0, 0))
+        assert text.get_antialiased() == default
+        assert annotation.get_antialiased() == default
+        assert explicit.get_antialiased() == (not default)
+    with mpl.rc_context({'text.antialiased': not default}):
+        assert text.get_antialiased() == default
+        assert annotation.get_antialiased() == default
+        assert explicit.get_antialiased() == (not default)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize('cls', [Text, Annotation])
+def test_text_antialiasing_properties(cls):
+    args = ('sample', (0, 0)) if cls is Annotation else ()
+    text = cls(*args, antialiased=True)
+    text.stale = False
+    text.set_antialiased(False)
+    assert text.get_antialiased() is False
+    assert text.stale
+    text.set(aa=True)
+    assert text.get_antialiased() is True
+    text.update({'antialiased': False})
+    assert text.get_antialiased() is False
+    alias = cls(*args, aa=False)
+    assert alias.get_antialiased() is False
+    other = cls(*args, antialiased=True)
+    other.update_from(text)
+    assert other.get_antialiased() is False
+
+

+    # Transparent backgrounds make intermediate coverage directly observable.
+    with mpl.rc_context({'text.antialiased': not antialiased,
+                         'text.usetex': False}):

[ENH]: Add get/set_antialiased to Text objects
### Problem

Currently, Text objects always retrieve their antialiasing state via the global rcParams["text.antialias"], unlike other artists for which this can be configured on a per-artist basis via `set_antialiased` (and read via `set_antialiased`).

### Proposed solution

Add similar getters/setters on Text objects (also adjusting Annotations accordingly, if needed) and use that info in the drawing stage.

Should be relatively easy to implement, except that the slight fiddling needed with backends requires some understanding of backend code (I think we need to replace the access to `rcParams["text.antialiased"]` by going through the GraphicsContext state).
description:
## Summary
Add per-artist antialiasing control to Text, inherited by Annotation, using `get_antialiased()`, `set_antialiased()`, the `antialiased` constructor property, and the `aa` alias.

The global `text.antialiased` rcParam supplies the creation-time default. Drawing then transfers the stored artist setting to the graphics context, which Agg and Cairo use for text rendering. Mathtext accepts an explicit setting and includes the resolved value in its parser cache key, preventing raster reuse across opposite antialiasing settings. `update_from` preserves the property as well.

## Regression coverage
The new test file checks both boolean states and deliberately uses opposing global defaults to distinguish artist-local behavior from accidental rcParam lookup. It covers Text and Annotation construction, aliases, creation-time default capture, copying, and targeted stale-state transitions: changing the setting invalidates a clean artist, while assigning the unchanged setting leaves it clean.

Agg integration tests check graphics-context propagation and actual alpha-channel output for ordinary text and mathtext. Separate parser tests verify cache separation, reuse, and default resolution after an rcParam change. Tests use the explicit Agg canvas and numerical raster properties rather than GUI dependencies or image baselines.

## Scope
No global defaults are changed. The implementation follows the existing artist-to-graphics-context rendering model; the supported setter contract is boolean, consistent with the documented property.

description:
## Fix Unicode HTTP methods with binary request bodies on Python 2

Normalize the uppercased method to a native `str` when constructing the session's Request. On Python 2, leaving an ASCII method such as `u'POST'` as Unicode can promote httplib's serialized headers to Unicode; appending a multipart body containing non-ASCII bytes then raises UnicodeDecodeError. The conversion prevents that promotion without changing the supplied payload.

## Regression coverage

The added tests exercise Session.request through request preparation and the standard-library HTTP serializer, using an in-memory socket rather than an external service. They cover:

- Unicode uppercase and lowercase POST methods with a binary multipart upload.
- Native-string POST with the same upload.
- A Unicode method with a raw binary body.
- Unicode and native-string GET methods without a body.

Assertions check the native method type, uppercase request line, successful serialization, and preservation of binary payload bytes. The multipart tests include bytes that cannot be implicitly decoded as ASCII, reproducing the important condition in the report. The tests are compatible with Python 2.7 and Python 3 and require no network access.

## Scope

This is a narrowly scoped fix for ASCII HTTP method names supplied as Unicode on Python 2. It does not introduce support for non-ASCII HTTP method names. Python 3 bytes-valued methods are a separate compatibility limitation of unconditional `str()` coercion: they become a representation such as `"b'POST'"`. This patch should not be interpreted as resolving that distinct input case.

+import unittest
+
+try:
+    import httplib
+except ImportError:
+    import http.client as httplib
+
+from requests import Response, Session
+
+
+PAYLOAD = b'\x00\xcf\xff\x80binary-upload\r\n'
+
+
+class MemorySocket(object):
+    def __init__(self):
+        self.parts = []
+
+    def sendall(self, data):
+        self.parts.append(data)
+
+    def close(self):
+        pass
+
+
+class SerializingSession(Session):
+    """Use real HTTP serialization, but never open a network connection."""
+
+    def send(self, request, **kwargs):
+        self.prepared_request = request
+        socket = MemorySocket()
+        connection = httplib.HTTPConnection('example.invalid')
+        connection.sock = socket
+        try:
+            connection.request(request.method, request.path_url,
+                               body=request.body, headers=request.headers)
+            self.wire = b''.join(socket.parts)
+        finally:
+            connection.close()
+        response = Response()
+        response.status_code = 200
+        response.request = request
+        response.url = request.url
+        response._content = b''
+        return response
+
+
+class UnicodeMethodRegressionTests(unittest.TestCase):
+    def assert_serialized_method(self, session, expected):
+        self.assertIs(type(session.prepared_request.method), str)
+        self.assertEqual(session.prepared_request.method, expected)
+        self.assertTrue(session.wire.startswith(
+            expected.encode('ascii') + b' /upload HTTP/1.1\r\n'))
+
+    def check_multipart(self, method):
+        session = SerializingSession()
+        try:
+            response = session.request(
+                method, u'http://example.invalid/upload',
+                files={u'file': ('payload.bin', PAYLOAD,
+                                  'application/octet-stream')})
+            self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 200)
+            self.assert_serialized_method(session, 'POST')
+            self.assertIn('multipart/form-data',
+                          session.prepared_request.headers['Content-Type'])
+            self.assertIn(PAYLOAD, session.prepared_request.body)
+            self.assertIn(PAYLOAD, session.wire)
+        finally:
+            session.close()
+
+    def test_unicode_uppercase_post_binary_multipart(self):
+        self.check_multipart(u'POST')
+
+    def test_unicode_lowercase_post_binary_multipart(self):
+        self.check_multipart(u'post')
+
+    def test_native_string_post_binary_multipart(self):
+        self.check_multipart('POST')
+
+    def test_unicode_post_raw_binary_body(self):
+        session = SerializingSession()
+        try:
+            session.request(u'post', u'http://example.invalid/upload',
+                            data=PAYLOAD)
+            self.assert_serialized_method(session, 'POST')
+            self.assertEqual(session.prepared_request.body, PAYLOAD)
+            self.assertTrue(session.wire.endswith(PAYLOAD))
+        finally:
+            session.close()
+
+    def test_unicode_and_native_get_without_body(self):
+        for method in (u'get', 'get'):
+            session = SerializingSession()
+            try:
+                session.request(method, u'http://example.invalid/upload')
+                self.assert_serialized_method(session, 'GET')
+            finally:
+                session.close()
+
+
+if __name__ == '__main__':
+    unittest.main()

+    def __init__(self):
+        self.parts = []
+
+    def sendall(self, data):
+        self.parts.append(data)
+
+    def close(self):
+        pass

+    def __init__(self):
+        self.prepared = None
+        self.wire = None

+            connection.request(request.method, request.path_url,
+                               body=request.body,
+                               headers=dict(request.headers))
+            self.wire = b''.join(sock.parts)
+        finally:
+            connection.close()
+        response = Response()
+        response.status_code = 200
+        response._content = b''
+        response.request = request
+        response.url = request.url
+        return response
+

+        pass

+                                       **kwargs)

+        finally:
+            session.close()

+        self.assertEqual(adapter.prepared.method, method.upper())
+        expected = method.upper().encode('ascii')
+        self.assertTrue(adapter.wire.startswith(
+            expected + b' /upload HTTP/1.1\r\n'))
+        return adapter

+        for method in (u'POST', u'post', 'POST', 'post'):

+                                  'application/octet-stream')})

+                          adapter.prepared.headers['Content-Type'])

+            self.assertIn(b'Content-Type: multipart/form-data;', headers)
+            self.assertEqual(body, adapter.prepared.body)
+            self.assertIn(b'filename="payload.bin"', body)
+            self.assertIn(self.payload, body)

+        for method in (u'POST', u'post', 'POST'):
+            adapter = self.serialize(method, data=self.payload)
+            self.assertEqual(adapter.prepared.body, self.payload)
+            self.assertEqual(adapter.wire.split(b'\r\n\r\n', 1)[1],
+                             self.payload)

+        for method in (u'GET', u'get', 'GET'):
+            adapter = self.serialize(method)
+            self.assertIsNone(adapter.prepared.body)
+            self.assertEqual(adapter.wire.split(b'\r\n\r\n', 1)[1], b'')

+    unittest.main()

## Fix byte-valued HTTP methods in Session.request

On Python 3, `str(b'GET')` produces `"b'GET'"`, not the HTTP method `GET`. Clients that encode their arguments before calling Requests therefore send an unintended method. This patch decodes byte-valued methods before request preparation, while retaining the existing `builtin_str` conversion for other inputs.

### Behavior and scope
- UTF-8 byte methods such as `b'GET'` are decoded, then pass through the existing method normalization and preparation path.
- Text methods and custom ASCII method tokens retain their existing behavior.
- Undecodable bytes use the patch's explicit permissive policy: invalid UTF-8 bytes are discarded. For example, `b'G\xffET'` becomes `GET`. This is lossy normalization, not validation; callers requiring strict rejection must validate their inputs. The tests make this policy visible rather than leaving it implicit.
- On Python 2, decoding changes the intermediate byte-method representation to Unicode. The compatibility tests check the resulting prepared method and transport handoff without asserting that the intermediate type is unchanged.

### Tests
Adds an offline unittest suite exercising the real `Session.request` and request-preparation pipeline, replacing only the final network send. Coverage includes the reported `b'GET'` regression, lowercase normalization, standard and custom method tokens, unchanged text inputs, UTF-8 decoding, malformed UTF-8 fallback, and byte/text parity on the executing runtime. The test file uses Python-2-compatible syntax and no mocking dependency; it can be run on each supported interpreter to establish runtime compatibility.

No redirect, adapter, or response-handling code is changed.

## Fix binary request payload preparation

Preserve string and byte payloads in `RequestEncodingMixin._encode_params` instead of passing them through `to_native_string`. Request bodies are opaque payloads: decoding them can reject valid binary content or change the bytes sent to the server. This fixes the reported regression from 2.8.1 for `data=u"ööö".encode("utf-8")`, and also preserves arbitrary non-UTF-8 bodies.

Because URL parameters use the same helper, `prepare_url` now explicitly converts bytes-valued parameter strings to text before composing the URL. This separates body handling from URL handling: raw bodies remain bytes, while already-encoded URL parameter strings are interpreted as UTF-8. Arbitrary binary query values should be supplied as structured parameters, which are percent-encoded, or as an already percent-encoded ASCII query string; this change does not introduce an arbitrary-byte URL decoding policy.

## Regression coverage

Adds offline tests exercising the public request-preparation API and the shared helper:

- The exact reported UTF-8 PUT payload, arbitrary non-UTF-8 bytes, embedded NULs, and empty bodies.
- Byte preservation and correct Content-Length through both direct and session preparation.
- File-like payload passthrough.
- Bytes-valued URL parameter strings, with and without an existing query and fragment.
- UTF-8 query decoding followed by URL escaping.
- Safe percent-encoding of binary values supplied as structured parameters.
- Explicit characterization of the UTF-8 boundary for unescaped byte query strings.

No network service or httpbin availability is required.

+    request = Request('PUT', 'http://example.com/put', data=payload)
+    if via_session:
+        session = Session()
+        try:
+            prepared = session.prepare_request(request)
+        finally:
+            session.close()
+    else:
+        prepared = request.prepare()
+    # Empty data may be normalized to no body by request preparation.
+    if payload:
+        assert prepared.body is payload

+    prepared = Request('PUT', 'http://example.com/put', data=stream).prepare()

+    if existing_query:
+        url += '?original=yes'
+    url += '#section'
+    prepared = Request('GET', url, params=params).prepare()
+    expected = 'http://example.com/put?'
+    if existing_query:
+        expected += 'original=yes&'
+    expected += 'a=1&b=2#section'
+    assert prepared.url == expected
+    assert prepared.body is None

+def test_utf8_byte_query_becomes_escaped_url_text():
+    prepared = Request(
+        'GET', 'http://example.com/put',
+        params=u'name=\u00f6\u00f6\u00f6'.encode('utf-8')
+    ).prepare()
+    assert prepared.url == 'http://example.com/put?name=%C3%B6%C3%B6%C3%B6'
+
+
+def test_structured_binary_query_value_is_percent_encoded():
+    prepared = Request(
+        'GET', 'http://example.com/put', params=[('value', b'\xff\x00\x80')]
+    ).prepare()
+    assert prepared.url == 'http://example.com/put?value=%FF%00%80'
+
+
+def test_preescaped_binary_query_is_preserved():
+    prepared = Request(
+        'GET', 'http://example.com/put', params=b'value=%FF%00%80'
+    ).prepare()
+    assert prepared.url == 'http://example.com/put?value=%FF%00%80'
+

+def test_raw_byte_query_requires_utf8_unlike_opaque_body():
+    # URL parameter strings are text; binary values use structured parameters
+    # or percent escapes, as covered above. Bodies have no such restriction.
+    with pytest.raises(UnicodeDecodeError):

+    prepared = Request('PUT', 'http://example.com/put', data=b'value=\xff').prepare()
+    assert prepared.body == b'value=\xff'

## Summary
Preserve proxy URL credentials when `prepend_scheme_if_needed` reconstructs a parsed URL.

The URL parser exposes authentication separately from the host and port. Previously, reconstruction used only the latter, dropping `username:password@` before the adapter could derive proxy authentication. Reattach the parsed authentication component to the netloc so authenticated proxy URLs retain their credentials.

This addresses a credential-loss path consistent with the reported 407 response. It does not introduce Python-version-specific behavior or change TLS handling.

## Regression coverage
Adds focused, network-independent tests covering:
- Authenticated proxy URLs with explicit and inferred schemes.
- Preservation of existing schemes, ports, paths, queries, and fragments.
- Percent-encoded credentials, IPv6 proxy addresses, and username-only authentication.
- Unauthenticated URLs remaining unchanged apart from the intended scheme default.
- Requests' adapter producing the expected Basic `Proxy-Authorization` header from the normalized URL, including decoding percent-encoded credentials.

The authenticated URL cases fail before the fix because reconstruction discards userinfo. The tests require no paid proxy, external network, or credentials. They are suitable for running on Python 3.8.12 as well as other supported Python versions; they do not claim to reproduce a live proxy's version-specific behavior.

## Validation
Run `python -m pytest -q tests/test_proxy_auth_url_regression.py`.

## Summary
Fix credential loss when normalizing authenticated proxy URLs. `prepend_scheme_if_needed` parses userinfo separately from the host and port, but previously omitted that userinfo when reconstructing the URL. Reattach the parsed authentication component before reconstruction so the adapter can generate proxy authentication.

This is a narrow fix for a concrete cause of proxy authentication failures: credentials disappearing before Requests creates its proxy manager. It does not special-case Python versions, change TLS behavior, or claim to establish why a particular paid proxy behaved differently on Python 3.8.12.

## Regression coverage
Adds network-independent tests for explicit and inferred schemes, existing scheme preservation, encoded credentials, IPv6 addresses, username-only authentication, and URLs without credentials. Tests also exercise `HTTPAdapter.get_connection`, verifying that the normalized proxy URL reaches the proxy manager and produces the expected Basic `Proxy-Authorization` header without leaking that header into the prepared origin request.

The adapter tests use explicit `try/finally` cleanup with `adapter.close()`; they do not assume that `HTTPAdapter` implements the context-manager protocol. Creating connection pools does not send requests or require a running proxy.

Authenticated regression cases distinguish the patch from the previous implementation, which discarded userinfo. Unauthenticated cases guard existing normalization behavior.

## Validation
Run `python -m pytest -q tests/test_proxy_auth_url_regression.py`.

No paid proxy, external network, or real credentials are required.

description:
## Summary
Separate timedelta64 and datetime64 numeric conversion in `_ensure_numeric`. Timedeltas represent durations and must convert directly to nanoseconds; they must not take the absolute-datetime offset conversion path. The datetime64 branch remains unchanged.

## Regression coverage
The new test file reproduces the issue's exact datetime-valued DataArray, elapsed-time coordinate, and three-axis polynomial coefficients. It checks both distinct evaluation inputs explicitly:

- Evaluating the elapsed-time coordinate reproduces the six published rows of expected polynomial values.
- Passing the original datetime-valued DataArray evaluates its datetime data, not its coordinate labels, and is checked against an independent NumPy calculation using epoch nanoseconds. This documents the distinction in the original example rather than silently replacing its input structure.

Additional parameterized tests exercise negative, zero, positive, and nonzero-origin durations across multiple source units. Assertions normalize dimension order and verify coordinate preservation and that inputs are not mutated.

## Scope and limitations
This fixes duration conversion; it does not change `polyval` to evaluate coordinate labels instead of the supplied array's data. Consequently, reproducing the historical elapsed-time output from the example requires passing `azimuth_time.coords['azimuth_time']`. The fixed patch also contains an unused `timedelta_to_numeric` import, which remains a minor lint cleanup item. No test execution results are claimed.

+    )

description:
## Summary
Prevent chunk metadata inspection from materializing backend-lazy arrays.

The reported failure originates in `get_chunksizes`: evaluating `v.data` can cross the lazy indexing and cache wrappers and read the entire backend array merely to check for a `chunks` attribute. This change removes that access:

- When `encoding['chunks']` is available, inspect that metadata directly.
- Otherwise, check the underlying array for chunk support without evaluating `Variable.data`.
- Retain dimension consistency checks and the existing handling of ordinary, unencoded chunked arrays.

## Regression tests
The new standalone test module uses a backend array that raises on every read. It exercises cached and uncached lazy wrappers, encoded and unencoded variables, Dataset and DataArray access, repeated inspection, and conflicting metadata. Encoded results are checked against exact values, not just dimension names. Shapes include partial final storage chunks. Optional Dask tests verify complete logical chunk tuples and inconsistent-layout detection on the fallback path.

These tests need neither remote data nor a Zarr installation: they reproduce the backend-wrapper boundary responsible for the reported read directly, making accidental materialization a deterministic failure.

## API boundary
The encoding branch exposes nominal storage chunk sizes as recorded in encoding; it does not expand them into logical per-block tuples. For example, a stored chunk size of 4 for a dimension of length 10 remains 4 rather than `(4, 4, 2)`. Encoding also takes precedence when present. The tests make that behavior explicit rather than treating storage metadata as equivalent to a Dask layout. Consequently, this patch addresses the reported unwanted I/O, but normalization and precedence for encoded, rechunked arrays remain compatibility limitations.

## Scope
This fixes xarray's materialized coordinate representation without changing pandas' internal MultiIndex level storage or introducing a new public API.

## Summary
Apply the configured ignore rules while discovering inputs for `--recursive=y`.

Recursive discovery now checks directory basenames against `ignore` and `ignore-patterns`, and directory paths against `ignore-paths`, before discovering packages or yielding files. ## Regression coverage
The new test file exercises the actual `PyLinter._discover_files` generator with temporary filesystem trees, covering:
- All three ignore settings for directories and individual files.
- Ignored directories both with and without `__init__.py`.
- Exclusion of nested descendants while retaining unrelated files.
- Ignored starting directories.
- Basename regex matching versus full-path regex matching.
- Preservation of package discovery and explicitly supplied module inputs.

## Scope and limitation
This is a focused discovery fix, not a change to ignore defaults. In particular, the documented `^\.#` default should not be described as ignoring every dot-prefixed directory.

The existing string-prefix implementation of `skip_subtrees` is retained. Consequently, a sibling whose path starts with an ignored directory's path can also be skipped, depending on traversal order. +    """Keep each case independent of user configuration and ignore defaults."""
+    instance = PyLinter()
+    instance.config.ignore = []

+    instance.config.ignore_paths = []
+    return instance

+    path.write_text('"""A fixture module."""\n', encoding="utf-8")
+    return path

+    elif kind == "ignore_patterns":

+    else:

+
+

+

## Summary
Respect configured ignore rules during recursive input discovery. Directory and file basenames are checked against `ignore` and `ignore-patterns`; paths are checked against `ignore-paths`, using the existing regex helper.

The change preserves the division of responsibilities between discovery and module expansion: recursive discovery filters entries it finds, while explicitly supplied package directories continue through the existing expansion pipeline. Tests therefore cover both the discovery generator and the public CLI rather than treating every generator yield as a linted input.

## Regression coverage
The new test module covers:
- All three ignore options, for both directories and individual Python files.
- Ignored directories with and without `__init__.py`, including nested descendants.
- An explicitly supplied ignored package directory through the actual CLI.
- Unrelated files remaining linted, so an empty result cannot accidentally satisfy an exclusion assertion.
- Default Emacs-lock-directory exclusion.
- Invocation through the public CLI, exercising the instance-method call sites as well as downstream expansion.

The original report's statement about the default requires clarification: `^\.#` excludes Emacs lock names, not all dot-prefixed names. This patch does not change that default.

## Remaining limitation
The existing subtree bookkeeping uses string prefixes rather than path-component boundaries. A similarly prefixed sibling can consequently be skipped after an ignored directory. A strict expected-failure regression records this limitation explicitly; this PR does not claim to fix it.

+"""Regression coverage for recursive ignore handling at discovery and CLI level."""
+
+import json
+import os
+from pathlib import Path
+import re
+import subprocess
+import sys
+
+import pytest
+
+import pylint
+from pylint.lint import PyLinter
+
+
+def _write(root, relative):
+    path = root / relative
+    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    path.write_text('import re\n', encoding='utf-8')
+    return path
+
+
+def _configure(linter, option, value):
+    if option == 'ignore':
+        linter.config.ignore = [value]
+    elif option == 'ignore-patterns':
+        linter.config.ignore_patterns = [re.compile(value)]
+    else:
+        linter.config.ignore_paths = [re.compile(value)]
+
+
+def _cli(root, option_args, targets):
+    # Keep the checkout importable after switching the subprocess working directory.
+    env = os.environ.copy()
+    checkout = str(Path(pylint.__file__).resolve().parent.parent)
+    env['PYTHONPATH'] = os.pathsep.join(
+        part for part in (checkout, env.get('PYTHONPATH', '')) if part
+    )
+    result = subprocess.run(
+        [sys.executable, '-m', 'pylint', '--recursive=y', '--persistent=n',
+         '--disable=all', '--enable=unused-import', '--reports=n', '--score=n',
+         '--output-format=json', *option_args, *targets],
+        cwd=str(root), env=env, capture_output=True, text=True, check=False,
+    )
+    assert result.returncode == 4, (result.stdout, result.stderr)
+    messages = json.loads(result.stdout)
+    assert messages
+    assert all(message['symbol'] == 'unused-import' for message in messages)
+    return {Path(message['path']).name for message in messages}
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize('option,value', [
+    ('ignore', 'excluded'),
+    ('ignore-patterns', '^excluded$'),
+    ('ignore-paths', r'.*[\\/]excluded$'),
+])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize('package', [False, True])
+def test_recursive_directory_ignores(tmp_path, option, value, package):
+    _write(tmp_path, 'visible.py')
+    _write(tmp_path, 'excluded/hidden.py')
+    _write(tmp_path, 'excluded/deeper/also_hidden.py')
+    if package:
+        _write(tmp_path, 'excluded/__init__.py')
+    linter = PyLinter()
+    _configure(linter, option, value)
+    discovered = set(linter._discover_files([str(tmp_path)]))
+    assert discovered == {str(tmp_path / 'visible.py')}
+    assert _cli(tmp_path, [f'--{option}={value}'], ['.']) == {'visible.py'}
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize('option,value', [
+    ('ignore', 'hidden.py'),
+    ('ignore-patterns', r'^hidden\.py$'),
+    ('ignore-paths', r'.*[\\/]hidden\.py$'),
+])
+def test_recursive_file_ignores(tmp_path, option, value):
+    _write(tmp_path, 'visible.py')
+    _write(tmp_path, 'nested/hidden.py')
+    _write(tmp_path, 'nested/retained.py')
+    linter = PyLinter()
+    _configure(linter, option, value)
+    discovered = set(linter._discover_files([str(tmp_path)]))
+    assert discovered == {
+        str(tmp_path / 'visible.py'), str(tmp_path / 'nested/retained.py')
+    }
+    assert _cli(tmp_path, [f'--{option}={value}'], ['.']) == {
+        'visible.py', 'retained.py'
+    }
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize('option,value', [
+    ('ignore', 'excluded'),
+    ('ignore-patterns', '^excluded$'),
+    ('ignore-paths', r'.*[\\/]excluded$'),
+])

+    _write(tmp_path, 'excluded/__init__.py')
+    _write(tmp_path, 'excluded/hidden.py')
+    _write(tmp_path, 'visible.py')
+    assert _cli(
+        tmp_path, [f'--{option}={value}'], ['excluded', 'visible.py']
+    ) == {'visible.py'}
+
+
+def test_default_lock_directory_pattern(tmp_path):
+    _write(tmp_path, '.#locked/hidden.py')
+    _write(tmp_path, 'visible.py')
+    assert _cli(tmp_path, [], ['.']) == {'visible.py'}
+
+
+@pytest.mark.xfail(
+    strict=True,
+    reason='Subtree tracking uses string prefixes, not path-component boundaries',
+)
+def test_ignored_directory_does_not_hide_prefixed_sibling(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
+    ignored = tmp_path / 'excluded'
+    sibling = tmp_path / 'excluded_extra'
+    ignored.mkdir()
+    _write(tmp_path, 'excluded_extra/visible.py')
+    # Specify traversal order so the boundary regression is filesystem-independent.
+    walk = [
+        (str(tmp_path), ['excluded', 'excluded_extra'], []),
+        (str(ignored), [], []),
+        (str(sibling), [], ['visible.py']),
+    ]
+    monkeypatch.setattr('pylint.lint.pylinter.os.walk', lambda *a, **kw: iter(walk))
+    linter = PyLinter()
+    _configure(linter, 'ignore', 'excluded')
+    assert set(linter._discover_files([str(tmp_path)])) == {
+        str(sibling / 'visible.py')
+    }

+"""Regression coverage for ignore settings during recursive discovery."""
+
+from pathlib import Path
+import os
+import re
+import subprocess
+import sys
+
+import pytest
+
+from pylint.lint import PyLinter
+
+
+def _write(path: Path, text: str = "import re\n") -> Path:
+    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    path.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
+    return path
+
+
+def _rule(option: str, target: Path) -> str:
+    if option == "ignore":
+        return target.name
+    if option == "ignore-patterns":
+        return "^" + re.escape(target.name) + "$"
+    return re.escape(str(target))
+
+
+def _tree(root: Path, kind: str):
+    keep = _write(root / "retained.py")
+    if kind == "file":
+        target = _write(root / "excluded.py")
+    else:
+        target = root / "excluded"
+        _write(target / "omitted.py")
+        _write(target / "nested" / "descendant.py")
+        if kind == "package":
+            _write(target / "__init__.py", '"""Excluded package."""\n')
+    return keep, target
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("option", ["ignore", "ignore-patterns", "ignore-paths"])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("kind", ["file", "directory", "package"])
+def test_recursive_discovery_filters_entries(tmp_path, option, kind):
+    root = tmp_path / "source"
+    keep, target = _tree(root, kind)
+    linter = PyLinter()
+    linter.set_option(option, _rule(option, target))
+
+    assert {Path(p) for p in linter._discover_files([str(root)])} == {keep}
+
+
+def _cli(tmp_path: Path, target: Path, options):
+    rcfile = tmp_path / "isolated.pylintrc"
+    rcfile.write_text("[MASTER]\n", encoding="utf-8")
+    result = subprocess.run(
+        [
+            sys.executable,
+            "-m",
+            "pylint",
+            "--rcfile=" + str(rcfile),
+            "--recursive=y",
+            "--disable=all",
+            "--enable=unused-import",
+            "--reports=n",
+            "--score=n",
+            "--persistent=n",
+            "--jobs=1",
+            "--msg-template={path}:{symbol}",
+            *options,
+            str(target),
+        ],
+        cwd=str(tmp_path),
+        capture_output=True,
+        text=True,
+        check=False,
+    )
+    return result
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("option", ["ignore", "ignore-patterns", "ignore-paths"])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("kind", ["file", "directory", "package"])
+def test_recursive_cli_filters_entries(tmp_path, option, kind):
+    root = tmp_path / "source"
+    keep, target = _tree(root, kind)
+    result = _cli(tmp_path, root, ["--" + option + "=" + _rule(option, target)])
+
+    assert result.returncode == 4, result.stdout + result.stderr
+    messages = [line for line in result.stdout.splitlines() if line.endswith(":unused-import")]
+    assert len(messages) == 1, result.stdout + result.stderr
+    assert keep.name in messages[0]
+    assert "excluded" not in messages[0]
+
+
+def test_default_pattern_excludes_lock_directory_not_all_hidden_directories(tmp_path):
+    root = tmp_path / "source"
+    keep = _write(root / "retained.py")
+    hidden = _write(root / ".ordinary" / "visible.py")
+    _write(root / ".#lock" / "omitted.py")
+    _write(root / ".#lock" / "nested" / "descendant.py")
+    _write(root / ".#locked.py")
+    linter = PyLinter()
+
+    assert {Path(p) for p in linter._discover_files([str(root)])} == {keep, hidden}
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("option", ["ignore", "ignore-patterns", "ignore-paths"])
+def test_explicit_ignored_package_is_filtered_by_cli(tmp_path, option):
+    package = tmp_path / "excluded"
+    _write(package / "__init__.py", '"""Package."""\n')
+    _write(package / "omitted.py")
+    result = _cli(tmp_path, package, ["--" + option + "=" + _rule(option, package)])
+
+    # An empty target set can produce Pylint's no-files status; neither outcome
+    # may emit the warning deliberately present in the ignored package.
+    assert result.returncode in (0, 32), result.stdout + result.stderr
+    assert ":unused-import" not in result.stdout
+
+
+def test_recursive_discovery_keeps_unignored_package_as_one_target(tmp_path):
+    root = tmp_path / "source"
+    package = root / "package"
+    _write(package / "__init__.py", '"""Package."""\n')
+    _write(package / "module.py")
+    keep = _write(root / "retained.py")
+    linter = PyLinter()
+
+    assert {os.path.normpath(p) for p in linter._discover_files([str(root)])} == {
+        os.path.normpath(str(package)),
+        os.path.normpath(str(keep)),
+    }

Paths are created using the host filesystem, exercising native Windows separators on Windows and POSIX paths elsewhere.

## Scope
The implementation is limited to path representation at the two existing ignore-path checks; traversal, module discovery, and diagnostic behavior are otherwise unchanged.

## Summary
Normalize native filesystem paths before applying `ignore-paths` at both existing filtering points in module expansion. On Windows, this allows forward-slash patterns such as `^src/gen/.*$` to match paths produced by recursive discovery.

The change deliberately leaves basename-based `ignore` and `ignore-patterns` checks, regex matching semantics, traversal, and module naming unchanged.

## Path representation
`Path.as_posix()` provides a platform-aware lexical representation without resolving paths, consulting the filesystem, changing case, or making paths absolute. It also collapses redundant separators and `.` components while preserving `..`. The regression tests explicitly document these behaviors. On POSIX, a literal backslash remains a filename character rather than being incorrectly treated as a separator.

Anchored expressions continue to match the supplied path representation: a relative pattern is not implicitly rebased onto an absolute path.

## Regression tests
The new test file includes:
- End-to-end CLI tests using the reported `pyproject.toml` setting and `--recursive=y src/`, for both ordinary directories and Python packages.
- A control invocation proving that both handwritten and generated files are discovered before the ignore rule is enabled.
- Exact diagnostic comparisons proving that generated files disappear while handwritten files remain checked.
- Focused checks for native separators, lexical normalization, retained parent components, unchanged basename exclusions, and nonmatching paths.

Tests use actual native filesystem paths; Windows execution therefore exercises Windows separators without replacing production path handling with a mock.

## Fix comma-separated regex options with repetition quantifiers

Preserve commas inside brace-delimited repetition quantifiers when converting regex-list options. Previously, `(foo{1,3})` was split into invalid fragments before regex compilation, causing configuration initialization to fail.

The converter continues to split top-level commas, strip surrounding whitespace, and compile each entry through the existing `_regex_transformer`. This applies to options using the shared regex-list converter, including `bad-names-rgxs`.

### Regression coverage

Adds focused tests exercising the actual converter for:
- The exact reported `(foo{1,3})` reproducer, including matching behavior.
- Bounded and open-ended repetition ranges.
- Multiple regex entries containing multiple quantifiers.
- Whitespace around list entries and ordinary comma-separated patterns.
- Empty input and invalid-regex error handling through the existing compiler.

Run with `python -m pytest tests/config/test_regexp_csv_quantifiers.py`.

### Scope

This is a targeted fix for commas in repetition quantifiers, not a new escaping or quoting grammar for regex lists. Commas in character classes, escaped commas, and escaped or literal braces remain limitations of this approach and should receive separate parser work. The root-level `foo.py` is a manual reproduction fixture; the new tests provide automated regression coverage independent of that file.

This change keeps commas inside braces in the same entry, while retaining top-level commas as separators between patterns. Compilation continues through `_regex_transformer`.

The new tests cover:
- The exact reported pattern, including its compiled matching behavior.
- Bounded and open-ended quantifiers, multiple quantifiers, and multiple list entries.

This fixes the reported repetition-range failure. It is not a complete regex-aware CSV tokenizer: escaped braces, unbalanced literal braces, and commas in character classes remain outside the supported improvement. The tests assert supported behavior directly without marking unsupported cases as expected failures.

+import json
+
+import pytest
+
+from _pytest._code.code import ExceptionChainRepr
+from _pytest.reports import TestReport
+
+
+CAUSE = "The above exception was the direct cause of the following exception:"
+CONTEXT = "During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred:"
+
+
+def raise_example(kind):
+    if kind == "single":
+        raise ValueError("outer-marker")
+    try:
+        try:
+            raise ValueError("inner-marker")
+        except ValueError as inner:
+            if kind == "explicit":
+                raise ValueError("middle-marker") from inner
+            raise ValueError("middle-marker")
+    except ValueError as middle:
+        if kind == "explicit":
+            raise ValueError("outer-marker") from middle
+        if kind == "suppressed":
+            raise ValueError("outer-marker") from None
+        raise ValueError("outer-marker")
+
+
+def make_report(kind, style):
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError) as excinfo:
+        raise_example(kind)
+    longrepr = excinfo.getrepr(style=style, showlocals=True)
+    longrepr.addsection("transport-section", "section-marker")
+    return TestReport(
+        nodeid="example.py::test_failure",
+        location=("example.py", 0, "test_failure"),
+        keywords={},
+        outcome="failed",
+        longrepr=longrepr,
+        when="call",
+        sections=[("Captured stdout call", "captured-marker")],
+        duration=0.01,
+    )
+
+
+def roundtrip(report):
+    # JSON, unlike an in-memory dict handoff, also converts chain tuples to lists.
+    wire = json.loads(json.dumps(report._to_json()))
+    return TestReport._from_json(wire)
+
+

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("kind", ["explicit", "implicit", "suppressed", "single"])
+def test_exception_chain_json_roundtrip(kind, style):
+    report = make_report(kind, style)
+    before = str(report.longrepr)
+    serialized_before = json.dumps(report._to_json(), sort_keys=True)
+    restored = roundtrip(report)
+
+    assert str(restored.longrepr) == before
+    assert restored.nodeid == report.nodeid
+    assert restored.outcome == "failed"
+    assert restored.when == "call"
+    assert restored.sections == report.sections
+    assert restored.longrepr.sections == report.longrepr.sections
+    assert "section-marker" in str(restored.longrepr)
+    assert json.dumps(report._to_json(), sort_keys=True) == serialized_before
+    assert str(roundtrip(restored).longrepr) == before

The change is confined to report serialization. Shared helpers handle traceback entries and crash locations consistently for both chained and non-chained representations, and report sections remain intact.

## Regression tests
The new tests exercise real exception representations through `TestReport._to_json()`, JSON encoding/decoding, and `TestReport._from_json()`, without an optional xdist dependency. They cover three-level explicit causes, implicit contexts, suppressed contexts, ordinary exceptions, and long/short traceback styles. Assertions check complete rendered-output equality, chain ordering and separator counts, crash metadata, sections, and repeat transport. A separate test exercises the non-chain `ReprExceptionInfo` branch.

## Transport compatibility
The serialization API is marked experimental. This patch supports round trips between producers and consumers using the updated schema; it does not add migration support for historical serialized dictionaries missing `chain`. That limitation is distinct from the reported same-version distributed-runner failure, which this change addresses. No backward-compatibility claim is made for stored reports or mixed-version transport.

+import copy
+import json
+
+import pytest
+
+from _pytest._code.code import ExceptionChainRepr, ExceptionInfo, ReprExceptionInfo
+from _pytest.reports import TestReport
+
+
+CAUSE = 'The above exception was the direct cause of the following exception:'
+CONTEXT = 'During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred:'
+
+
+def _explicit(marker):
+    try:
+        try:
+            raise ValueError(marker + '-first')
+        except ValueError as first:
+            raise TypeError(marker + '-second') from first
+    except TypeError as second:
+        raise RuntimeError(marker + '-last') from second
+
+
+def _implicit(marker):
+    try:
+        try:
+            raise ValueError(marker + '-first')
+        except ValueError:
+            raise TypeError(marker + '-second')
+    except TypeError:
+        raise RuntimeError(marker + '-last')
+
+
+def _suppressed(marker):
+    try:
+        raise ValueError(marker + '-hidden')
+    except ValueError:
+        raise RuntimeError(marker + '-last') from None
+
+
+def _ordinary(marker):
+    raise RuntimeError(marker + '-last')
+
+
+def _representation(raiser, style):
+    try:
+        raiser('transport-probe')
+    except Exception:
+        info = ExceptionInfo.from_current()
+    return info.getrepr(style=style, showlocals=True, funcargs=True)
+
+
+def _report(longrepr):
+    return TestReport(
+        nodeid='test_transport.py::test_failure',
+        location=('test_transport.py', 0, 'test_failure'),
+        keywords={},
+        outcome='failed',
+        longrepr=longrepr,
+        when='call',
+        sections=[('Captured stdout call', 'captured output\n')],
+        duration=0.125,
+    )
+
+
+def _crash(crash):
+    return crash.path, crash.lineno, crash.message
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize('style', ['long', 'short'])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    'raiser,separator,count',
+    [(_explicit, CAUSE, 3), (_implicit, CONTEXT, 3),
+     (_suppressed, None, 1), (_ordinary, None, 1)],
+)
+def test_exception_chain_survives_json_transport(raiser, separator, count, style):
+    original = _representation(raiser, style)
+    original.addsection('Diagnostic details', 'additional details')
+    expected = str(original)
+    assert isinstance(original, ExceptionChainRepr)
+    assert len(original.chain) == count
+    assert expected.count(CAUSE) == (count - 1 if separator == CAUSE else 0)
+    assert expected.count(CONTEXT) == (count - 1 if separator == CONTEXT else 0)
+    messages = [part[1].message for part in original.chain]
+    if count == 3:
+        assert messages == [
+            'ValueError: transport-probe-first',
+            'TypeError: transport-probe-second',
+            'RuntimeError: transport-probe-last',
+        ]
+    else:
+        assert messages == ['RuntimeError: transport-probe-last']
+    expected_crashes = [_crash(part[1]) for part in original.chain]
+    expected_separators = [part[2] for part in original.chain]
+    report = _report(original)

+        assert payload == snapshot
+        # A decoded transport dictionary can be consumed more than once.
+        assert str(TestReport._from_json(payload).longrepr) == expected
+        assert isinstance(restored.longrepr, ExceptionChainRepr)
+        assert str(restored.longrepr) == expected
+        assert len(restored.longrepr.chain) == count
+        assert [_crash(part[1]) for part in restored.longrepr.chain] == expected_crashes
+        assert [part[2] for part in restored.longrepr.chain] == expected_separators
+        assert _crash(restored.longrepr.reprcrash) == expected_crashes[-1]
+        assert restored.longrepr.sections == original.sections
+        assert restored.sections == report.sections
+        assert restored.nodeid == report.nodeid
+        assert restored.location == report.location or tuple(restored.location) == tuple(report.location)
+        assert restored.outcome == 'failed'
+        assert restored.when == 'call'
+        assert restored.duration == 0.125
+        assert str(original) == expected
+        report = restored
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize('style', ['long', 'short'])
+def test_non_chain_exception_representation_survives_json_transport(style):
+    chained = _representation(_ordinary, style)
+    plain = ReprExceptionInfo(chained.reprtraceback, chained.reprcrash)
+    plain.addsection('Diagnostic details', 'plain exception details')

+    report = _report(plain)

+        assert not isinstance(report.longrepr, ExceptionChainRepr)

## Summary
Defer mounting a package until collection actually finds a Python module to collect. Merely walking past a directory containing `__init__.py` must not import that package: unrelated packages may legitimately require a different platform or unavailable dependencies.

The change retains mounting and package fixture discovery for collected modules, including the case where `__init__.py` itself matches `python_files`.

## Regression coverage
Adds subprocess-based collection tests covering:
- An unrelated package whose initializer raises, alongside a passing standalone test.
- An unrelated package containing non-test Python files and a nested package whose initializer also raises.
- A real test package with two test modules consuming a fixture defined in its initializer, exercising fixture discovery across repeated collection iterations.
- Explicit configuration that includes `__init__.py` in `python_files`, ensuring initializer tests are still collected.

The negative cases assert successful collection and execution rather than merely checking that an error message disappears. Subprocess isolation prevents package imports from leaking between scenarios.

## Scope
This addresses eager imports during package traversal; it does not suppress import failures in packages that actually contain collected tests. The commented-out eager mount marks the lifecycle operation that has moved to the collection branches. Repeated fixture discovery is exercised by the multi-module package test.

description:
## Summary
Avoid importing unrelated packages merely because collection traverses their directories. Package mounting is deferred until a collector is actually produced, or until the initializer itself matches `python_files`. Fixture discovery remains associated with mounted packages.

This fixes the reported case where a platform-specific package raises on import even though none of its files are tests. Import errors in packages that really contain tests remain visible.

## Validation
Adds isolated subprocess regressions for:
- The original failing initializer alongside an ordinary passing test.
- Unrelated packages containing ordinary Python files and nested packages.
- Collection-only traversal, proving that avoiding execution alone is not the fix.
- Package fixtures consumed by multiple collected modules, including teardown.
- Package `setup_module` and `teardown_module` lifecycle behavior across multiple modules.
- Explicit initializer collection through `python_files`.
- Import failures in packages containing actual tests, which must still fail collection.

Assertions check exit status and test outcomes; lifecycle tests additionally verify persisted event logs after subprocess termination. No runtime dependencies or public interfaces are added.

## Implementation notes
The explicit loop replaces `yield from` so mounting and fixture discovery occur before each relevant collector is yielded. The commented former eager-mount call identifies the operation relocated into those branches; it has no runtime effect. The tests focus on observable collection and lifecycle behavior rather than depending on private collector implementation details.

description:
## Summary
Defer package initialization until collection actually produces a relevant collector. Merely traversing an unrelated package no longer imports its `__init__.py`, fixing the pytest 5.2.3 regression affecting platform-specific packages.

Packages containing tests still initialize before their collectors are yielded. Initializers matching `python_files` remain collectable, and import errors in packages containing real tests remain visible.

## Regression coverage
The new test file exercises:
- An ordinary passing test beside unrelated packages whose initializers raise, including nested packages and non-test Python files.
- Both ordinary execution and `--collect-only`.
- Explicit initializer collection through `python_files`.
- Import failures in packages that actually contain tests.
- Package fixture discovery across multiple test modules, with direct checks that repeated discovery does not duplicate fixture definitions.
- Session-scoped package fixture setup and teardown occurring exactly once, verified using an event file after subprocess exit.

## Implementation details
Mounting and fixture discovery happen before each relevant collector is yielded. Repeated calls to `parsefactories` use the fixture manager's existing holder-deduplication behavior; the regression test checks the resulting registration count as well as fixture execution. No new runtime dependency or public API is introduced.

The commented former eager-mount call is an inert remnant, not a second initialization path. It is a cosmetic cleanup opportunity; the behavioral change is confined to when package initialization and fixture discovery occur.
